When AI gets the details wrong in your field, real people pay for it. The people who know the work best have to be the ones training these models. You’re not being replaced by AI. You’re making sure it’s used accurately and safely.

Design challenging, realistic electrical and electronics engineering problems based on professional practice, such as circuit specifications, control-loop stabilization, and power-stage sizing.

Fluency in English at a native or bilingual level.
At least 2 years of industry experience in circuit or electronics engineering.
Background in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, or a closely related discipline.
Strong command of circuit analysis, design tradeoffs, and component-level and system-level decision-making.
Ability to clearly explain why an engineering answer is incorrect, not only identify that it is incorrect.
Comfort using AI tools or ability to learn them quickly.
A current, in-progress, or completed Bachelor's degree is preferred but not required.
Must be located in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, or the United States.

Quantitative Trading

The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories’ technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems.

The Electric Propulsion & Plasma Science section focuses on experimentally studying electric propulsion and other low-temperature plasma space technologies. The Center for Perinatal Discovery (CPD) is a collaboration between the Departments of Pathology, Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Sciences, and Pediatrics.
